findings.evidence: False positive for the data type: no user-created or user-provided audio is involved. The audio is public hero voice lines from the app's response catalog (VOResponse.Body.audioUrl). ResponseRingtoneSetter.kt:83 only reads it, from a local file or by URL(response.audioUrl).openStream(), which is an inbound download with no user data in a request body. Lines 57-79 copy it into the local MediaStore and line 42 calls RingtoneManager.setActualDefaultRingtoneUri, both on-device. The flow runs only from the user's action in the response sheet (ResponsesFragment.kt:125, onSetAs at line 90), after the user grants the write-settings permission on the system screen (lines 127-131). The strings.xml hits (dialog_response_set_ringtone, hero_response_ringtone_set) are UI labels only. No upload sink exists on this path.
findings.recommendation: No action needed and no Data Safety declaration needed for audio. Revisit if the app ever records or uploads user audio.

findings.evidence: False positive for the data type: all three hits are Gradle build tooling that runs on the developer's machine and is not packaged in the app. IncludeModulesPlugin.kt:16,19 only names the micro-benchmark and macro-benchmark modules for settings inclusion. BranchComparisonPlugin.kt:19 registers the benchmarkBranchComparison task, applied from the root build.gradle.kts:3,19-25 with target task :app:help. BranchComparisonTask.kt:116-125 runs a local gradle-profiler and writes reports to the local gradle/profiler/last-output directory (lines 167-168). This measures build times, not app users, and has no network sink. A search of the .toml and .kts build files found no Firebase, Crashlytics, AppMetrica, Sentry, Mixpanel, Amplitude, AppsFlyer, Bugsnag or play-services-ads dependency.
findings.recommendation: No action needed and no Data Safety declaration needed for app performance data.
